blocked_scoped_locales.mn-Mong: Existing traditional Mongolian terms establish canvas and original size, but the new finite/passive clauses and traditional-script suffix forms have not been verified. Mechanical Cyrillic transliteration would not establish correct written Mongolian. See research-v2/v2-review-index.md for the second-pass clause evidence and exact remaining grammar/terminology questions.
blocked_scoped_locales.jje: The catalogue gives Jeju endings and terms, but they do not establish authentic Jeju predicates for declaration, usability, and canvas-derived substitution. Merely changing South Korean sentence endings would be unsupported. See research-v2/v2-review-index.md for the second-pass clause evidence and exact remaining grammar/terminology questions.
blocked_scoped_locales.mnc-Mong: Existing Manchu terms for drawing area and original size are available; the syntax and technical wording for usable declared dimensions, substitution, and Android bitmap limits are not verified. Mongolian text or invented script strings are not proposed. See research-v2/v2-review-index.md for the second-pass clause evidence and exact remaining grammar/terminology questions.
blocked_scoped_locales.ain-Kana: The paired catalogue supplies カㇺピソ / ホㇱキ ポロル and an existing no-automatic-resize phrase. The argument structure for an SVG declaring dimensions and passive substitution is not established; Japanese clauses written in kana would be invalid. See research-v2/v2-review-index.md for the second-pass clause evidence and exact remaining grammar/terminology questions.
blocked_scoped_locales.ain-Latn: The paired catalogue supplies Kampiso / Hoski pororu and the existing size-warning scaffold. New predicate valency and negative substitution syntax are unverified; a wordwise conversion from Japanese or a guessed Latin sentence is withheld. See research-v2/v2-review-index.md for the second-pass clause evidence and exact remaining grammar/terminology questions.
blocked_scoped_locales.ryu: Existing Okinawan 元ぬサイズ and no-resize wording do not establish the new declaration and canvas-based substitution predicates. Standard Japanese with a few Okinawan particles/endings would not be a responsibly supported translation. See research-v2/v2-review-index.md for the second-pass clause evidence and exact remaining grammar/terminology questions.
